audits.title: EGS P12 An audit of local management of upper gastrointestinal bleeds in a UK district general hospital
audits.standard: NICE quality standards / CG141 for acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding

cycle1.result: Blatchford score used in 12.5% (5/40); endoscopy <24 hours in stable patients 91.4% (32/35); PPI for non-variceal bleeds 74.4% (29/39); aspirin stopped 60% (3/5); immediate endoscopy in unstable patients 100% (4/4).

audits.intervention: Education of doctors about the NICE quality standards for AUGIB management over a 1-year interval.

cycle2.result: Blatchford score used in 50% (11/22); endoscopy <24 hours in stable patients 53% (10/19); PPI for non-variceal bleeds 77% (17/22); aspirin stopped 80% (4/5); immediate endoscopy in unstable patients 100% (3/3).

audits.other_findings: Endoscopic management was fully compliant in both cycles (clips 100%; variceal bleeds all given terlipressin, antibiotics and band ligation). Time to endoscopy in stable patients worsened.
audits.citation: Patel A, Simpson K, Duffy N, Tan W, Kassam R. EGS P12 An audit of local management of upper gastrointestinal bleeds in a UK district general hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac404.077.

audits.title: 560 Stop the Bleed: Audit of the Management of Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding at Cavan General Hospital, Republic of Ireland
audits.standard: NICE CG141, QS38 and BSG guidelines: GBS risk stratification, endoscopy within 24 hours (variceal within 12 hours), terlipressin and antibiotics for variceal bleeds

cycle1.result: 100% vital signs and IV access, 97% fluid resuscitation; GBS not documented in most cases; PPI ~98%; endoscopy in 85% but only 63% within 24 hours (mean delay 42.8 h); only 1/5 variceal cases within 12 hours; variceal bleeds: 50% terlipressin, 83% antibiotics.

audits.other_findings: Transfusion practice appropriately restrictive (mean pre-transfusion Hb 7.5 g/dL). A UGIB proforma and checklists are being introduced with re-audit planned within 12 months.
audits.citation: Butt A, Chishti S, Nzewi E. 560 Stop the Bleed: Audit of the Management of Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding at Cavan General Hospital, Republic of Ireland. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.229.

audits.title: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the UK: 2022 audit update.
audits.standard: UK guidelines for acute upper GI bleeding, including pre-endoscopic risk stratification and restrictive transfusion thresholds

cycle1.result: Transfusion rate 43%; inpatient endoscopy 74%; endotherapy 23%; rebleeding 13.3%; in-hospital mortality 10.0%.

cycle2.result: Pre-endoscopic risk stratification not performed in 42%; transfusion rate 50%; of early transfusions 43% given at Hb > 70 g/L and 24% inappropriate; inpatient endoscopy 83%; endotherapy 27%; rebleeding 9.7%; mortality 8.8%.

audits.other_findings: Inappropriate transfusion at 80 g/L was linked with higher adjusted mortality (aOR 1.60); patients in 2022 had more comorbidity, cirrhosis and anticoagulant use than in 2007.
audits.citation: Nigam GB, Oakland K, Hearnshaw S, Grasnt-Casey J, Davies P, Dhiman P, et al.. Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the UK: 2022 audit update. Gut. 2026;75(4):760-771. doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2025-335134. PMID: 41260910.

audits.title: Use of endoscopy for management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the UK: results of a nationwide audit.
audits.standard: Published standards for endoscopy in acute upper GI bleeding
audits.setting: 208 UK hospitals accepting acute upper GI bleeding admissions (national audit)

cycle1.result: 74% had inpatient endoscopy, 50% of these within 24 h; only 55% of high-risk patients (Rockall >=5) endoscoped within 24 h and 14% waited >=72 h; 74% of high-risk lesions received endoscopic therapy.

audits.other_findings: Consultant-led out-of-hours rota in 52% of hospitals; risk-adjusted mortality ratio 1.21 (p=0.10) in hospitals without such rotas; mortality 7.4% in those endoscoped.
audits.citation: Hearnshaw SA, Logan RF, Lowe D, Travis SP, Murphy MF, Palmer KR. Use of endoscopy for management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the UK: results of a nationwide audit. Gut. 2010;59(8):1022-1029. doi:10.1136/gut.2008.174599. PMID: 20357318.

audits.title: Using an 'action set' for the management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
audits.standard: National standard for acute upper GI bleeding management ('Scope for improvement' report)

cycle1.result: Inappropriate pre-endoscopy PPI 73.8%; post-OGD PPI 66%; discharge of patients with full Rockall 2 or less 40%.

audits.intervention: Local guidelines, presentations and an electronic 'Action Set' in the Cerner Millennium record system.

cycle2.result: Pre-OGD Rockall documentation increased significantly (p 0.0001 or less); post-OGD full Rockall improved (p = 0.007); inappropriate pre-endoscopy PPI 33% (p = 0.02); post-OGD PPI 50% (p = 0.01); low-risk discharge 100% (p = 0.43).

audits.citation: Pericleous M, Murray C, Hamilton M, Epstein O, Negus R, Peachey T, et al.. Using an 'action set' for the management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Ther Adv Gastroenterol. 2013;6(6):426-437. doi:10.1177/1756283x13496971. PMID: 24179478.
